title: Residual generic points and components under arbitrary field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $L/k$ be any field extension [def-weil-field; def-pc-field-extension]. Let $Z$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] and form $p:Z_L=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For any $w\in Z_L$, put $z=p(w)$. The fibre of $p$ over $z$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(z)\otimes_kL)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre; def-weil-residue-field; def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product; def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $w$ is generic in an irreducible component of $Z_L$ if and only if $z$ is generic in an irreducible component of $Z$ and the point of $w$ in this residual fibre is generic in an irreducible component of that fibre [def-sc-generic-point; def-weil-irreducible-components]. In this case $E=\overline{\{w\}}\subseteq Z_L$ is an irreducible component; for every closed immersion $j:T\hookrightarrow Z_L$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] and point $v\in T$ with $j(v)=w$, one has $j(\overline{\{v\}})=E$, and $v$ is generic in an irreducible component of $T$. No algebraicity, separability, finite type, Noetherianity or reducedness hypotheses are imposed.

proof.text: We first spell out the elementary topological reduction. For a point $a$ of a scheme $H$ and an open neighbourhood $U$, the closure $D=\overline{\{a\}}$ is an irreducible component of $H$ exactly when $D\cap U$ is an irreducible component of $U$. Indeed, a larger irreducible closed subset of $U$ has irreducible closure in $H$ containing $D$. Conversely, if an irreducible closed $C$ strictly contains $D$, then $C\cap U$ strictly contains $D\cap U$: the nonempty open $C\cap U$ is dense in $C$, so containment in the closed $D$ would force $C\subseteq D$. Choose $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Since $\overline{\{\mathfrak r\}}=V(\mathfrak r)$ directly from the Zariski closed sets, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] identifies component-generic points of $U$ with minimal primes. Moreover $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$ in $U$ means $\mathfrak r_b\subseteq\mathfrak r_a$. Every generalization $b$ of $a$ lies in $U$ (every open containing $a$ contains $b$). Consequently, in any scheme, $a$ is component generic if and only if it has no proper generalization: $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$ implies $b=a$. This uses no finiteness assumption.

source.place: Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible), parts (1) and (3); the open-locality and generalization arguments are written out here.

proof.text: The defining fibre product of the fibre $F_z=(Z_L)_z$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$. To check this, a map into either scheme is the same pair of maps into $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L$ with equal composites to $\operatorname{Spec}k$; the map to $Z$ is forced to be the canonical map through $z$. The unique maps supplied by these universal properties are inverse because they preserve both projections. The affine fibre-product lemma therefore identifies $F_z$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(z)\otimes_kL)$, with its canonical point corresponding to $w$. The fibre definition also identifies its underlying space homeomorphically with $p^{-1}(z)$ with the subspace topology. Thus for $w'\in p^{-1}(z)$, the corresponding fibre point generalizes the fibre point of $w$ exactly when $w\in\overline{\{w'\}}$ in $Z_L$: closure in a subspace is ambient closure intersected with that subspace.

source.place: Tag 05DC (lemma-base-change-relative-assassin), proof: displayed residual-fibre identification; universal-property argument without its local-finite-type hypothesis.

proof.text: For the image assertion choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Z$ containing $z$. By the open fibre-product and affine fibre-product lemmas, $p^{-1}(U)=U_L$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B=A\otimes_kL$, and its map to $U$ is induced by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat]; its base change $U_L\to U$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. The affine flatness criterion then says $A\to B$ is a flat ring map. Write $\mathfrak q$ for the prime of $w$ in $B$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$ for the prime of $z$ in $A$. These arguments apply to an arbitrary field extension and an arbitrary affine $k$-algebra.

source.place: Tags 01U9 (lemma-base-change-flat), 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); affine charts from schemes.tex, Tags 01JR and 01I4.

proof.text: Suppose $w$ is component generic in $Z_L$. Step 1 makes $\mathfrak q$ a minimal prime of $B$. If a prime $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ existed in $A$, flat going-down would give a prime $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak p_0$. Minimality forces $\mathfrak q_0=\mathfrak q$, contradicting their different contractions. Thus $\mathfrak p$ is minimal, and step 1 makes $z$ component generic in $Z$. Any generalization of the point of $w$ in $F_z$ gives, by step 2, a generalization of $w$ in $Z_L$, hence is $w$ by step 1. Applying step 1 to the scheme $F_z$ proves that the fibre point is component generic as well.

source.place: Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down), applied to the flat affine scalar-extension map in step 3.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $z$ and the point of $w$ in $F_z$ are component generic. If $w'$ generalizes $w$ in $Z_L$, continuity of $p$ implies that $p(w')$ generalizes $z$: the inverse image of every open containing $z$ contains $w$ and therefore $w'$. Step 1 gives $p(w')=z$. Step 2 now makes $w'$ a generalization of $w$ inside $F_z$, so step 1 in that fibre gives $w'=w$. Step 1 in $Z_L$ concludes that $w$ is component generic. This proves the equivalence in the statement.

source.place: Elementary closure and subspace argument using the criteria proved in steps 1 and 2; generic-point definition Tag 004X.

proof.text: In this case $E=\overline{\{w\}}$ is an irreducible component by the definition of a generic point of a component. A closed immersion $j:T\hookrightarrow Z_L$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subspace, so that subspace contains $E$ when it contains $w$. Closure of a singleton in a subspace is its ambient closure intersected with the subspace. Consequently $j(\overline{\{v\}})=E$. Finally, an irreducible subset of $T$ strictly containing $\overline{\{v\}}$ would, under this homeomorphism, be an irreducible subset of $Z_L$ strictly containing $E$, contradicting maximality of the component $E$. Thus $\overline{\{v\}}$ is an irreducible component of $T$ and $v$ its generic point. This argument uses the topology of a closed immersion and imposes no condition on its defining ideal or on nilpotents.

source.place: Definition Tag 01IO (closed immersion); elementary closed-subspace closure and maximality argument.
